<reason>Side B made the easier decision rule: public naming confers present honor, history lives in archives and curricula, and “primarily” can separate founders from Confederate generals. Side A’s residue/orientation frame and new-versus-inherited distinction were philosophically sharp, and its pressure on majority-flip instability plus the keep-vote fork actually damaged B. But A never neutralized the meaning/harm double bind or matched the lived-cost claim, while B’s limited-class case remained clearer than A’s standing-default continuity.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO R1 trap: CON needs names to be priceless when removed and harmless when kept (B2.1–B2.2), which structured the rest of the clash.</best_rebuttal>
